changes: Amṛtānanda: roles scribe+commentator changed to reader. In Newari, 'jātakamālāvyākhyā … yāṅā … saṃpūrṇaṃ' records a ritual recitation and exposition (vyākhyāna) of the text that ran from Śrāvaṇa śu 1 to Bhādrapada kṛ 9. It does not record copying or writing a commentary.
Pūrṇānanda: roles scribe+other changed to reader, because the same vyākhyā formula is used. Amarāvatī moved out of residence: it is where the reading took place, not a stated home.
No scribe is named in the colophon. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Amṛtānanda? Pūrṇānanda?' is a misreading of the reading notes.
Date: kept NS 894 as the earliest dated entry. Noted that it dates a reading, so it is only a terminus ante quem for the copying. Added the second date to the notes.
Place emptied: Amarāvatī nagara is where the 927 reading took place, not where the copy was made.
Purpose cut back to the merit formula only.

purpose: merit for the welfare of the world (jagaddhite)
notes: The scribal colophon is badly damaged and names no scribe. The dated Newari entries after it are reading notes. (1) NS 894 (1774 CE): Amṛtānanda began a vyākhyā (recitation and exposition) of the Mahajjātakamālā on Śrāvaṇa śu 1, Monday, and finished it on Bhādrapada kṛ 9. Dhanasiṃha is named in a gap and his role is unclear; he may have been the patron or a listener. (2) NS 927 (1807 CE), Āśvina śu 15, Friday: Pūrṇānanda gave a Jātakamālā vyākhyā in the city called Amarāvatī (nugasa = 'in the centre'?). The place is not identified; Amarāvatī may be a poetic name for a Newar town. Jagajjitānanda's role is lost in a lacuna. The copy was therefore made in or before NS 894. The catalogue's scribe and date fields probably come from these notes. Amṛtānanda may be the well-known paṇḍita Amṛtānanda (fl. late 18th to early 19th century), but this is not certain.
